name: MGJ2D151515SC
title: MGJ2 series: 2 W DC-DC converters with 5.2 kVDC isolation and bipolar outputs for gate drives
summary: A family of 2 W isolated DC-DC converters in a five-pin SIP, each giving a positive and a negative rail about a shared 0V for driving IGBT and MOSFET gates. Inputs are 5, 12, 15 or 24 V nominal; output pairs are +15 V with -3, -5, -8.7 or -15 V, +17 V/-9 V, +18 V with -2.5 or -5 V, and +20 V with -3.5 or -5 V. The barrier is hi-pot tested at 5.2 kVDC, holds 2.4 kVDC continuously as functional isolation and couples 3 to 4 pF; the series is UL62368-1 recognised, and ANSI/AAMI ES60601-1 recognised except for the variants listed as pending, MGJ2Dxx1515SC among them. MGJ2D151515SC is the 15 V input, +15 V/-15 V, 67 mA per output variant, now discontinued.

circuits.title: Differential mode noise test schematic
circuits.description: Bench set-up for the output ripple and noise figures. The converter runs from a supply whose negative side is earthed and drives a resistive load at full rated power over twisted wires. A 1 µF ceramic and a 10 µF tantalum sit across the output; the signal goes through a 100 nF capacitor and a 450 Ω resistor into coax wound three turns through a ferrite toroid, ending in a 50 Ω termination at the oscilloscope input, whose ground is earthed. The reading is multiplied by 10.

operation.text: Isolated supplies for the high-side and low-side gate drivers of IGBT and MOSFET bridges, such as those of inverters and motor drives. Each variant gives an asymmetric pair of rails, one positive and one negative, about a common 0V. CMTI is characterised as greater than 200kV/μs, and partial discharge performance is characterised.

Every unit is hi-pot tested at 5.2kVDC for 1 second in production; qualification is at 5.2kVDC for 1 minute. Repeated high-voltage testing can wear the barrier down; where a retest cannot be avoided, it is run at 20% below the specified test voltage.
Used as functional (non-safety) isolation, the barrier holds continuous or switched voltages up to 2.4kV. The figure rests on partial discharge inception measurements to IEC 60270.
There is no fuse inside. UL use needs an anti-surge, UL-recognised fuse in the input line: 1.25A for 5 V input types and 750mA for 12 V, 15 V and 24 V input types.
Specifications hold from 10% load upward, over the whole input range. Below 10% load the output voltage rises, typically up to 1.25 times its nominal value once the load drops under 5%.
With an input rising in 2.2μs and 10μF on the output, start-up takes 2.5 to 21 ms depending on variant. The converters also start into 47μF to 220μF of output capacitance, taking longer to do so.
Each envelope bounds the output voltage deviation from nominal over 10% to 100% load, combining set point accuracy and load regulation; positive and negative outputs have their own envelopes.

Cooling is by free air convection. Full output current is available to 85°C ambient for 051515, 051802, 052003, 121503, 121515 and 151515, to 95°C for 051505, 052005, 121802, 122003, 151802, 152003, 241802 and 242003, and to 100°C for the rest.
The pin finish is hot-dipped tin over matte tin, with a nickel preplate. The parts suit RoHS wave soldering at 260ºC peak for 10 seconds and are also compatible with Sn/Pb processes.

MGJ 2 D XX XXXX S C: MGJ is the series, 2 the power rating, D the output type (S single, D dual, T triple, Q quad), XX the input voltage, XXXX the output voltages, S the package (S SIP, D DIP, M surface mount, Z ZIP) and C marks RoHS compliance.
The case carries the order code (MGJ2DXXXXXXSC) and a date code XYYWW.
